sections.html: Corydoras fulleri Tencatt, Santos, Evers & Britto, 2021. Common names: C115, Fuller's Cory, C116. Size: 65 mm (2.6") SL. C115 = C116: captive breeding has shown these two C-numbers to be the same, highly variable species. C115 lacks the mid-body blotch, C116 has it.

Rio Madre de Dios, Peru. Amazon, Middle Amazon (Solimoes), Madeira, Madre de Dios. Type locality: stream tributary of the upper río Manuripe (or Manuripi), locally known as Alegría, a tributary of the río Orthon, rio Madeira basin, Las Piedras, Tambopata, Madre de Dios, Peru.

Ideally substrate should be sand, but rounded gravel is an imperfect alternative. Avoid rough-edged (chipped) gravel, which increases the risk of damage to the fish's barbels when it digs. Substrate should be bordered with driftwood and aquatic plants, leaving an open area to search for food and swim. Shade from overhanging rock work, arching bogwood, and tall or floating plants is all that is required to settle these fish.

Readily accepts all prepared foods that reach the bottom of the aquarium, such as tablets, granules and larger flakes. Live or frozen foods such as bloodworm, white worm, grindal worm (Enchytraeus), Daphnia and Tubifex are readily accepted and good for conditioning groups of fish for spawning.
Females grow larger and are more full-bodied, best observed from above. Males typically have more pointed rather than rounded fin tips as they mature.

Corydoras are identified by their twin rows of armour plates along the flanks and by having fewer than 10 dorsal fin rays. They are most commonly confused with the other genera in the sub-family, namely Brochis, Scleromystax and Aspidoras. Named in honour of Ian A. M. Fuller, an aquarist who devoted most of his life to keeping and breeding Corydoradinae species. IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated.
Journal of Fish Biology v. 99 (no. 2), pp 2 [615], Figs. 1-4.
